newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end sharply off on Dow jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end sharply off on Dow jitters.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended earlier losses to close sharply lower on Wednesday on the back of a sliding Dow Jones Industrial Average, lack of foreign investor interest and sales of stocks by local investors ahead of Thursday's holiday, traders and analysts said.
"The bourse was very weak. New York hurt us most as it made local and foreign investors nervous," said Daniel Romo, research chief at the Bancrecer bank.
The blue chip IPC index .MXX ended off 65.31 points, or 1.98 percent, at 3,241.75. points. A preliminary close level was slightly lower.

The Dow Jones average meanwhile closed down 1.09 percent at 6,402.52 points. Analysts said both U.S. and Mexican stocks began to slide after U.S. long bond rates gained in the wake of a higher than expected rise in the producer price index.
Some traders attributed the late slide to dealers selling stocks to stay liquid over the national Virgin of Guadalupe holiday on Thursday.
"No one knows what the Dow Jones will do tomorrow, so some preferred to go liquid and step out," said one trader.
On the broad market, 96 stocks changed hands, as losers trounced gainers by 72 to six.
One notable gainer was steelmaker Grupo IMSA, which concluded an Initial Public Offering Wednesday. IMSA closed at 17.00 pesos, or 37 centavos above its issue price.
Debt-stricken holding group Sidek headed the losers after closing down 11 centavos at 71.
Technical analysts noted the IPC closed below support at 3,250 points, but said it had yet to confirm a breakthrough at this level.
